references.text: Reuben tore his clothes when he discovered that Joseph was missing from the well – a direct parallel in the same family story.
Jacob tore his clothes when he thought Joseph was dead. The same expression of grief in Joseph's family story.
Joshua and Caleb tore their clothes in despair over the people's rebellion – the same action as a sign of deep sorrow.
David and his men tore their clothes in mourning over the death of Saul and Jonathan.
Job tore his robe when he learned about the death of his children – tearing clothes as an expression of extreme grief.
Direct narrative continuation: Describes the same group and action (loading donkeys) in immediate chronological order.
